In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of stochastic partial differential equations with non-differentiable noise is now well understood.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a pathwise semigroup theory for non-differentiable noise.
we have been able to extend the classical theory of parabolic equations and transport equations to the non-differentiable setting.
we have developed a pathwise theory for nonlinear parabolic equations driven by fractional noise of sufficiently high regular order, which includes the case of the white noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regularity of the solution is governed by the regularity of noise, and that this is true for all regularities of the noise that are not too small.
, in the non-differentiable setting, the semigroup approach is a viable alternative to the more traditional approach based on stochastic calculus.
, in many cases, the pathwise methods are more efficient than the probabilistic methods, which are based on the theory of martingale problems.
